raw_case_text:
RJS, a 30-year-old woman, was seen at the health post of Corte de Pedra, Tancredo Neves:Bahia, a reference center for diagnosis and treatment of CL. The patient complained of a small papular lesion in her right leg developing over seven to 10 days. When she was 10 years of age, she had an ulcer in the left thigh suspicious of CL that spontaneously healed in about 4 months. Given her prior history of ulcer, she decided to seek help at the health post when the new lesion appeared. On physical examination, a depressed papular lesion measuring 8 x 7 mm in the right leg suspicious of folliculitis was noted. There was also a well-defined atrophic scar in the left thigh, measuring 30 x 20 mm (Figure 1). There was no lymphadenopathy. Because early CL lesions in L. braziliensis infection may have a papular and nonulcerated aspect and the patient lived in an endemic area, the diagnosis of CL was suspected. LST was prepared as previously described. Briefly promastigotes of L. amazonensis were disrupted initially by multiple freeze and thaw and later by sonication. The material was adjusted to 250 mug/mL with sterile PBS containing Tween 80 and phenol. An intradermal injection of 0.1 mL was administered in her left forearm. After 48 hours, the intradermal reaction was highly positive with an induration of 38 x 32 mm. Eight days after the skin test, while the folliculitis in the right leg disappeared, a cutaneous round ulcer with raised borders measuring 26 x 24 mm, typical of leishmaniasis, was observed in the site where the LST was administered (Figure 2). The clinical picture was typical of an ulcerated CL lesion, but the culture of the aspirated material from this lesion was negative for Leishmania. The histopathological analysis (Figure 3) showed chronic perivascular inflammation with granuloma formation and the presence of neutrophils, lymphocyte, monocyte, and plasma cells. Parasites were not identified, but a few amastigote forms were detected by immunohistochemical analysis performed with rabbit anti-Leishmania braziliensis antibody in skin sections. 
Determination of cytokine production was performed by ELISA (R&D Systems, Minneapolis, Minn, USA) in supernatants of peripheral blood mononuclear cells stimulated with soluble Leishmania antigen (SLA) for 72 hours. TNF-alpha and IFN-gamma levels were 47 pg/mL and 0 pg/mL, respectively, in unstimulated cultures and were 2,943 pg/mL and 2,313 pg/mL, respectively, in SLA-stimulated cultures. These values were similar to those detected in 3 patients with CL who were evaluated on the same day: TNF-alpha: 2,139 +- 953.8; IFN-gamma: 3,653 +- 312.6. The patient was treated with pentavalent antimony (Glucantime) in a dosage of 20 mg/kg/day and pentoxifylline 400 mg tid for 20 days. Pentoxifylline has anti-inflammatory properties, and it has been previously shown that its use in combination with antimony is more effective than antimony alone in the treatment of tegumentary leishmaniasis. The ulcerated lesion in the left forearm was completely healed 40 days after the initiation of therapy (Figure 4).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 30-year-old female presented with a small papular skin lesion on her right lower leg of 7 to 10 days duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a new small papular lesion on her right leg that developed over 7 to 10 days. Because of a prior childhood experience with a self-healing skin ulcer, she sought early medical evaluation at a reference health post.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of a self-resolving ulcer on the left thigh at 10 years of age that healed spontaneously over 4 months, leaving an atrophic scar. Epidemiological history: resident of Corte de Pedra, Bahia, Brazil (an endemic area for tegumentary leishmaniasis).
subjective.review_of_systems: Denies systemic symptoms, fevers, or pain outside the cutaneous findings.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic examination revealed a depressed papular lesion measuring 8 mm x 7 mm on the right leg suspicious for folliculitis, and a well-defined atrophic scar measuring 30 mm x 20 mm on the left thigh. No regional lymphadenopathy was palpable.
objective.routine_investigations: Supernatants of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) stimulated with soluble antigen for 72 hours revealed TNF-alpha of 2,943 pg/mL (vs. 47 pg/mL unstimulated) and IFN-gamma of 2,313 pg/mL (vs. 0 pg/mL unstimulated).
objective.advanced_workup: Histopathological examination of induced forearm ulcer: chronic perivascular inflammation with granuloma formation composed of neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and plasma cells; routine microscopy did not visualize parasites. Culture of aspirate from forearm lesion: negative for growth.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Intradermal leishmanin skin test (LST) yielded a strongly positive reaction of 38 mm x 32 mm induration at 48 hours, followed by ulceration at the injection site. Immunohistochemical analysis of the forearm ulcer biopsy using rabbit anti-Leishmania braziliensis antibody identified Leishmania amastigotes, confirming cutaneous leishmaniasis (exaggerated hypersensitivity response triggered by skin testing). Bacterial folliculitis resolved spontaneously. Management and Outcome: Treated with intravenous/intramuscular pentavalent antimony (Glucantime) 20 mg/kg/day combined with oral pentoxifylline 400 mg three times daily for 20 days. Complete healing of the forearm ulcer was achieved 40 days after treatment initiation.
